related_questions.question: Are home COVID tests still accurate?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, at-home COVID tests, specifically antigen tests, are generally considered accurate, particularly when someone has symptoms. Positive results are usually reliable. However, they may be less sensitive at detecting the virus early in an infection or in asymptomatic individuals. It's recommended to repeat testing following a negative result to reduce the risk of a false negative.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, at-home COVID tests, specifically antigen tests, are generally considered accurate, particularly when someone has symptoms

list.snippet: Symptomatic individuals: At-home antigen tests are quite effective at detecting COVID-19 when someone is experiencing symptoms. For example, a study found that BinaxNOW tests detected nearly 90% of symptomatic cases.
Asymptomatic individuals: Antigen tests are less sensitive at detecting the virus in people who don't have symptoms.
Positive results: Positive results from at-home antigen tests are generally reliable.
Negative results: If you get a negative result, it's recommended to repeat the test to reduce the chance of a false negative.

Types of tests: There are two main types of at-home tests: antigen tests and molecular tests. Antigen tests are rapid and produce results quickly, while molecular tests (like PCR tests) are more sensitive but require sending a sample to a lab.
Where to get tests: At-home COVID-19 tests are available online and in stores.

related_questions.question: Can I take a COVID test at home?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, you can test for COVID-19 at home using over-the-counter (OTC) rapid antigen tests. These tests are widely available at pharmacies and online retailers. They provide results in minutes and can help you quickly determine if you have an active COVID-19 infection.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, you can test for COVID-19 at home using over-the-counter (OTC) rapid antigen tests

text_blocks.snippet: How to use at-home COVID-19 tests:

list.title: Purchase a test:
list.snippet: Buy an FDA-authorized at-home COVID-19 test kit from a reputable source like a pharmacy or online retailer.

list.title: Follow the instructions:
list.snippet: Carefully read and follow the instructions provided with the specific test kit you purchased.

list.title: Perform the test:
list.snippet: Collect your sample (usually a nasal swab) and perform the test according to the instructions.

list.title: Read the results:
list.snippet: Most tests provide results within minutes. Follow the instructions on how to interpret the results.
If you have symptoms of COVID-19, such as fever, cough, sore throat, or fatigue, it's recommended to test as soon as possible.
If you've been exposed to someone with COVID-19, testing is also recommended, especially if you have symptoms or are at higher risk of severe illness.
Testing can help you make informed decisions about whether to isolate yourself to prevent further spread of the virus.

list.title: Follow-up testing:
list.snippet: If your at-home test is positive, it's recommended to confirm the results with a PCR test, especially if you are at higher risk of severe illness.

list.title: Consult with a healthcare professional:
list.snippet: If you have questions or concerns about your results, or if you are experiencing severe symptoms, consult with a healthcare professional.

list.title: Check expiration dates:
list.snippet: Regularly check the expiration dates of your at-home test kits, as some may have extended expiration dates, according to the Mayo Clinic.
